short: The largest battle of the civil wars, which permanently shattered Royalist power in northern England.
full:
On 2 July 1644, a combined force of English Parliamentarians and Scottish Covenanters defeated the Royalist army at Marston Moor outside York. Seeking to relieve the besieged city of York, Prince Rupert boldly marched a Royalist relief force to confront the larger allied army. The battle unfolded in the early evening, with a devastating Parliamentarian cavalry charge led by Oliver Cromwell rolling up the Royalist right flank.

Despite fierce Royalist resistance and a counter-charge that briefly threatened to break the allied lines, the discipline of the Parliamentarian cavalry proved decisive. The Royalist army lost over 4,000 men and a significant portion of its artillery and officer corps. The crushing defeat lost King Charles I control of northern England and paved the way for Parliament's total victory in the First English Civil War.
